$comment: Machine-readable summary of the Operational AI Assurance Framework (OAAF) v1.0. The full text (FRAMEWORK.md / PDF) is authoritative.
name: Operational AI Assurance Framework
author: Armend Verbovci
summary: A free, sector-neutral method for deciding, on evidence, whether a deployed AI system or AI agent should keep operating, be restricted, or be stopped, adapted from aviation safety management.
principles: System of operation: assurance applies to the AI-enabled system as deployed and operated, not the model alone.
Context dependency: operational risk depends on context, not capability.
Continuous, not one-off: assurance is maintained for the life of the system through continuous, periodic and event-triggered activity.
Assurance is not performance: good performance figures are not evidence that degradation would be noticed.
Acceptable, not absolute: the objective is acceptable operation within a defined context and risk tolerance.
Accountability requires authority: an owner who cannot restrict or stop the system is a control deficiency.
Negative-space assurance: assurance must cover what the system does not flag, escalate or surface.

capability_criticality.q1: Human acceptance: must a human positively accept this specific output before it takes effect? Visibility, sampling or after-the-fact intervention do not count.
capability_criticality.q2: Consequence: if the output is wrong, would the harm be irreversible before it would normally be detected, or exceed the materiality threshold? Judge reversibility of the consequence, not of the action.
capability_criticality.default_materiality: Where no threshold is set, any consequence that moves money, commits the organisation to a third party or communicates externally on its behalf is material.
capability_criticality.note: An attribute used only to set the minimum tier and to rate findings. Not a second tier system.

2.harm: Operational disruption, material financial loss, recoverable harm to individuals
2.autonomy: Meaningful autonomy with a human in the loop

3.harm: Severe or irreversible harm to people, critical services or the organisation
3.autonomy: Limited or no practical override window

rules: A system with any High capability is at least Tier 2.
Regulatory classification is recorded separately as an overlay and does not set the tier.

control_states.name: Degraded
control_states.meaning: Operating conditions or assurance margin deteriorated, within tolerance

control_states.name: Restricted
control_states.meaning: Operation permitted only with added controls, such as human acceptance or reduced limits

control_states.name: Contained
control_states.meaning: Capability constrained, isolated or on fallback

control_states.name: Unacceptable
control_states.meaning: Continued operation exceeds accepted risk; stop the affected capability
control_states.typical_authority: Accountable owner or anyone with stop authority

control_state_notes: States are defined for both model condition and service condition (availability, stale data, monitoring outage, dependency failure).
Leaving S3 or S4 requires return to service (P5-04).

requirements.requirement: A named individual is designated as accountable owner of the deployed system.
Technical, risk and business responsibilities for the system are documented and assigned to named roles.
An escalation path from the accountable owner to senior management is documented.
An accountability statement sets out the responsibilities of suppliers, model providers and deployers.

(a) The accountable owner holds documented authority to initiate restriction or stopping of any capability; and (b) a mechanism exists to execute it within a response time set for each capability, and it has been exercised within the review period.
Foreseeable misuse and credible failure modes relevant to the operating context are documented.
typical_evidence: Hazard list on the System Card

requirements.requirement: Structured hazard identification covers model, data, integration, infrastructure, human-factors and external-dependency failure modes, including hazards whose controls are owned by other functions (see the Boundary Rule, 7.2).
typical_evidence: Hazard log with owner and interface recorded for each hazard

requirements.requirement: Risk is assessed using a documented method covering at least severity and likelihood, and where relevant detectability and control effectiveness.
The risk record is reviewed at a defined interval of no more than 12 months, and after every material change and every occurrence classed as Deviation or above.
Conditions requiring restriction, containment or cessation of operation are documented and provided to the accountable owner.
typical_evidence: Operating limits on the System Card

requirements.requirement: Operational control states are defined for this system, covering both model condition and service condition, including fail-safe or fail-open behaviour when the AI is unavailable.
Measurable trigger conditions are defined for each transition between states.
Decision authority is defined for each transition between states.
State transitions and their rationale are logged.
The system's technical permissions in other systems are limited to the capabilities declared in the System Definition. Any further permission is removed, or declared and assessed.
typical_evidence: Permission inventory compared with capability list

requirements.requirement: Operational performance is monitored and reviewed by a named person at a defined interval.
Safety-relevant indicators are distinguished from general performance indicators.
Targets and trigger levels are defined for safety-relevant indicators and linked to the state triggers in P3-03.

Assurance coverage is reported using hazard-signal mapping: for each hazard in the risk record, whether an operational signal exists that would detect it before harm (full, partial or none), reported as three counts. Interim method; see 9.2.
Both leading indicators (conditions that precede harm) and lagging indicators (harm and near misses that occurred) are tracked at a defined interval.
For each High capability, monitoring covers the path where output became action with no human acceptance, using sampling, outcome tracking or independent checks.
A channel exists for reporting problems with system output, and users and affected staff know how to use it.
Occurrences are classified using a taxonomy that distinguishes at least deviation, near miss and incident (see Annex F).
Occurrences classed as Deviation or above are investigated for cause, and corrective action is recorded.
A return-to-service process is defined and evidenced for any capability leaving S3 or S4.
Lessons from occurrences are fed into the risk record (P2) and the change process (P6).

A configuration baseline is maintained that is sufficient to reconstruct the system that produced any given output: model and version, prompts and instructions, tools and the permissions they used, data and knowledge sources, persistent memory or context stores, and thresholds.
The operational significance of each change is assessed and recorded before release, judged by its potential effect on behaviour, boundaries, controls or risk, not by its technical size.
Changes are classified by impact level (administrative, configuration, behavioural, functional, boundary, safety control), with evidence requirements that increase with impact.
Changes classed as behavioural or higher are re-assessed against the risk record and operational boundaries before release.

External dependencies that can materially change system behaviour, including model providers and third-party data, are subject to change detection, version pinning, supplier notification, or evidenced compensating monitoring, in proportion to their significance.
Every human role that receives, accepts or acts on system output is identified.
Risks of over-reliance and under-reliance are assessed for each such role.
Escalation authority and criteria are documented for each such role.
Competency requirements are defined and current for everyone holding intervention authority.
Degradation of oversight effectiveness is assessed, including workload, alert saturation, complacency and incentives that discourage challenge.

assessment_values.Compliant: Defined, in use, and a record shows it operating within the review period. At Tier 1, defined and in use is sufficient.
assessment_values.Partially Compliant: Defined but incomplete, inconsistently applied, or no record of operation.
assessment_values.Not Demonstrated: Evidence insufficient to establish that the control is defined and in use. Does not mean it does not exist.
assessment_values.Not Applicable: Requirement is above the system's Consequence Tier.

review_period: 12 months, or the time since the last material change, whichever is shorter.

evidence_rules.name: Evidenced, not assumed
evidence_rules.text: A control owned by another function counts only if evidenced against this system: a named owner, a record the assessor has seen, and a demonstrated link to this system's decision path. An assumed control is Not Demonstrated.

evidence_rules.name: Absence of harm is not evidence
evidence_rules.text: A clean incident record does not downgrade an unassessed risk, and is not evidence of control effectiveness where monitoring that would detect the harm is absent or of unknown coverage.

evidence_rules.name: Boundary Rule
evidence_rules.text: A hazard that can affect a capability's decision path must be recorded even when its control is owned by another function, naming the owning function and the interface.

finding_criticality.applies_to: Every Partially Compliant or Not Demonstrated result, rated separately for each capability it affects.
finding_criticality.adjustment: May be raised one level with written reasons; never lowered. Three levels only; no numeric score.

outcomes.Ready with Conditions: Significant findings, or Critical findings cleared by evidenced compensating control or time-limited risk acceptance, and no open Critical

clearing_critical: A documented, time-limited risk acceptance signed by someone holding authority under P1-05(a) to stop that capability
decision.not_ready_in_operation: Move the capability to S2 Restricted or S3 Contained until cleared.

assessment_triggers: Periodic review, at least every 12 months
Change classed as behavioural or higher
Proposal to retire, or capability no longer meets its purpose
